topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: A plant is biologically considered a weed when it ________.
options: Grows where it is not wanted
questions.explain: In agriculture, any plant that grows in a place where it is not desired and competes with cultivated crops is defined as a weed.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: A major characteristic of weed seeds that allows them to remain viable in the soil for a very long period until conditions are favorable is called ________.
questions.explain: Long dormancy is a characteristic of weeds that enables their seeds to survive in the soil for years under harsh conditions and only germinate when environmental conditions become favorable.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Weeds are notoriously difficult to control because they possess the characteristic of being easily dispersed by ________.
questions.explain: Many weed seeds are light, winged, or have hooks, which allows them to be easily dispersed over wide areas by wind, water, and passing animals.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Despite their negative impact on crops, some weeds are beneficial to humans primarily because they have ________.
questions.explain: Certain weeds (such as neem or lemongrass relatives, lemon weed) are used by herbalists and pharmaceutical industries for their medicinal properties to treat various ailments.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct benefit of certain weeds to livestock?
options: They act as a source of food (forage)
questions.explain: Many grassy and leguminous weeds serve as excellent sources of forage or pasture for feeding ruminant livestock like cattle and sheep.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: The method of weed control that involves planting different types of crops on the same piece of land in a sequential, regular order is known as ________.
questions.explain: Crop rotation involves growing different crops in succession on a specific piece of land. It helps disrupt the life cycle of specific weeds associated with particular crops.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Chemical substances applied on the farm specifically to kill or control the growth of weeds are called ________.
questions.explain: Herbicides are agricultural chemicals formulated specifically to kill unwanted plants (weeds). Insecticides kill insects, while fungicides destroy fungi.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: One of the major environmental hazards associated with the continuous and excessive use of chemical herbicides on the farm is the ________.
options: Pollution of soil and ground water
questions.explain: Chemical herbicides can wash away during rains or seep into the earth, leading to the pollution of the soil and underground water bodies.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: How can the careless application of chemical weed control methods negatively affect farm animals?
options: By increasing the animal's resistance to diseases
By stimulating milk production in dairy cows
By causing contamination of livestock pasture
By eradicating external parasites from their bodies
questions.explain: Applying herbicides without care can contaminate the pasture or forage that grazing animals feed on, which could lead to poisoning and death of the livestock.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: An insect pest that damages crops by using its modified mouthparts to pierce plant tissues and extract sap is classified as a ________.
questions.explain: Piercing and sucking insects possess tube-like mouthparts (proboscis) designed to pierce plant epidermal tissues and suck out the cellular sap.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Which of the following insect pests is a typical example of a biting and chewing insect?
questions.explain: Grasshoppers possess strong mandibles adapted for biting off and chewing plant leaves and stems.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Which group of insects is known for transmitting viral diseases to crops while feeding on them?
questions.explain: As piercing and sucking insects (like aphids and whiteflies) move from an infected plant to a healthy one to feed on sap, they often inject viruses into the healthy plant.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: The typical physical damage caused by biting and chewing insects on crop plants is ________.
options: Creation of ragged holes in the leaves
Wilting without any visible physical wounds
questions.explain: Because they eat solid plant tissues, biting and chewing insects leave distinct ragged holes and irregular edges on leaves and shoots.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: What is the primary effect of crop pests on agricultural production?
options: They speed up the maturity of crops
They reduce the quality and yield of crops
They improve the soil nutrient content
They decrease the cost of farming
questions.explain: Crop pests destroy plant tissues and compete with crops, which drastically reduces both the quality (market value) and the overall yield of the harvest.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Which of these describes how piercing and sucking insects primarily reduce crop yield?
options: By eating the roots of the crop entirely
By draining the plant of essential sap causing wilting and stunting
By cutting the stem of the seedlings at the soil level
By blocking sunlight from reaching the leaves
questions.explain: Piercing and sucking insects feed on the internal plant sap, robbing the plant of nutrients and water, which results in wilting, stunting, and low yield.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Weeds often outgrow cultivated crops primarily because they ________.
options: Are given special fertilizers by the farmer
Are naturally highly aggressive and competitive
Rely entirely on pests for survival
questions.explain: Weeds are naturally adapted to local environments and are highly aggressive, enabling them to outcompete crops for light, space, and nutrients.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: A characteristic of weed seeds that allows them to be carried easily by wind to distant farm lands is that they are ________.
options: Light and sometimes have wing-like structures
Able to swim through underground water
questions.explain: Many weed seeds are easily dispersed by the wind because they are tiny, light, and possess adaptations like wings or parachutes (pappi).
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Cotton stainers belong to which class of insect pests based on their mouth parts?
questions.explain: Cotton stainers possess piercing and sucking mouthparts which they use to pierce cotton bolls and extract sap, staining the lint in the process.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Which cultural method of weed control involves turning the soil to bury the weeds before planting?
questions.explain: Tillage (plowing and harrowing) turns the topsoil over, which helps in uprooting and burying existing weeds.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pests Control

questions.q: Which of the following refers to a chemical method of controlling insect pests on a farm?
questions.explain: Insecticides are chemicals specifically manufactured and applied to control or kill insect pests on crops.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
